record.field: tour store keeper guided daily loop receive issue return damage fifo scan walkthrough keeper
Walk through a Store Keeper's daily loop — receive, putaway, issue, return, damage.

div.h2: Your daily loop, one click at a time
div.p: This is the day in the life of a Store Keeper: stock comes in, it gets put away, it goes out for the cows and the pooja room, some comes back, and anything broken gets reported. Click each button to open the real screen, take a look, then come back here with the Back button.

img.alt: Receiving flow: scan, check, put away

ol.li:
Receive stock — a delivery arrives. Scan each item, tick the quality check, pick your name, and validate.
Open this screen →

Putaway — give the new stock its home. The system suggests a slot; here you can see all the Slots and how stock sits in them.
Open this screen →

Issue stock (FIFO) — hand stock out. The wizard tells you the exact slot to take from, oldest first.
Open this screen →

img.alt: FIFO issue: the oldest stock leaves first

ol.li:
Returns — a borrowed tool or unused spare comes back. Scan it back in so it's available again.
Open this screen →

Report damage — found something broken, expired, or spoiled? Move it off the shelf so nobody issues it by mistake.
Open this screen →

div.p: Nicely done — that's the whole loop. When you're ready for the detail behind each step, read:

ul.li: Keeper Path 1: Getting started as a Store Keeper (slug keeper-path-getting-started) — the full first-day walkthrough.
FIFO issuing workflow (slug workflow-fifo-issuing) — a step-by-step on taking stock out the right way.

record.field: tour admin manager guided setup build zone rack onboard products roster reports backup health walkthrough
Build and run the warehouse — zones, racks, products, people, reports, backups.

div.p: As an Admin you do two jobs: build the warehouse (zones, racks, products, people) and run it (watch the reports, keep the backups safe). This tour clicks through both, in order. Open each screen, have a look, then use Back to return here.

img.alt: Warehouse structure: Zone to Rack to Compartment to Slot

ol.li:
Create a Zone — a Zone is a room or area (Pharmacy, Feed Store). Start here so your racks have a home.
Open this screen →

Create a Rack — a Rack is one shelving unit, laid out as a grid of shelves and columns. The generator builds it and its slots for you.
Open this screen →

Onboard products — tell the system what the trust buys and uses (feed, medicine, ghee, tools), each with a clear SKU.
Open this screen →

img.alt: Roles and permissions: Manager, Store Keeper, and capability switches

ol.li:
Manage the storekeeper roster — add one row per real person so wizards can record who was on duty.
Open this screen →

Review reports — Slot Occupancy shows you, at a glance, how full the warehouse is.
Open this screen →

img.alt: Backup, restore drill, and health check

ol.li:
Check backups & health — the safety net. Confirm a recent backup ran and the weekly restore drill is passing.
Open this screen →

img.alt: Cloud backup: encrypted copy to Google Drive and the restore path back

ol.li:
Cloud safety net — every daily backup also lands in the trust's Google Drive, already encrypted. Run an extra one any time with Back Up Now; the schedule and tests live under Configuration → Google Drive Backup.
Open this screen →

div.p: That's the whole job — build and run. For the reasoning behind each part, read:

ul.li: Admin Path 1: What this system is and what it does (slug admin-path-system-overview) — the big picture before the detail.
Backup verification workflow (slug workflow-backup-verification) — how to be sure your data is truly safe.

A look-only tour of the live reports — occupancy, movements, expiry, and audits.

div.p: You're here to see what's going on, not to change it — and that's exactly right. Everything in this tour is read-only, so click freely: nothing you open can alter the stock. Open each screen, have a look, then use Back to return here.

ol.li:
Slot Occupancy — how full the warehouse is, slot by slot. Your best first glance.
Open this screen →

Movement history — every receipt, issue, and return: what moved, when, and who handled it.
Open this screen →

Oldest stock / FIFO — what has been sitting longest, so nothing is forgotten at the back of a rack.
Open this screen →

Expiry alerts — medicine, feed, and fluids that are close to their expiry date.
Open this screen →

Audit history — the inventory audits (counts) and how they turned out.
Open this screen →

div.p: That's everything you need to keep an eye on the store. To get more from the reports, read:

ul.li: Read-only Path: Using the reports (slug readonly-path-using-reports) — how to read each dashboard.
Read-only Path: Audit visibility (slug readonly-path-audit-visibility) — understanding the count history and the audit trail.
